articles.body: 여러 항목을 고르는 설문에서는 선택 건수를 더한 값이 응답자 수보다 클 수 있습니다. 예를 들어 여섯 사람이 열 번 체크했다면, 먼저 여러 항목을 고를 수 있는 문항이었는지 확인해야 합니다. 합계가 크다는 이유만으로 중복 응답을 지우면 정상적인 선택까지 빠질 수 있습니다. 아래 표는 공용 도구 사용 안내의 희망 형식을 집계합니다. 짧은 글·그림·영상은 각각 3명이 골라 응답자 기준으로는 50.0%이고, 형식 선택 9건을 기준으로는 각각 33.3%입니다. 입력 자료, 셀별 수식, 완성 결과와 빈 양식 재사용 순서를 제공합니다. 본문 작성과 DEV용 재구성에 AI를 사용했습니다. 예제는 합성 자료이며 실제 설문을 수집하거나 Excel에서 실행한 사례가 아닙니다. 수량·분모·빈 입력 조건은 Python으로 검산했습니다. 이 검산은 실제 앱 동작이나 사람의 검토를 수행했다는 뜻이 아닙니다. R01 같은 번호도 연습 자료의 행을 구분하는 값입니다. 1. 질문과 입력 기준을 먼저 고정하기 [합성 설문 한 문항] 공용 도구 사용 안내를 어떤 형식으로 받고 싶나요? 원하는 형식을 모두 고르세요. 선택지: 짧은 글 / 단계별 그림 / 짧은 영상 / 희망 없음 원하는 형식이 없으면 희망 없음만 고르세요. [문항 끝] 한 사람이 이 문항에 남긴 응답 하나를 한 행에 넣습니다. 선택은 숫자 1, 미선택은 숫자 0입니다. 세 형식은 함께 고를 수 있지만 “희망 없음”은 단독 선택입니다. 무응답은 희망 없음으로 바꾸지 않습니다. 이 예제의 여섯 행은 서로 다른 사람이 유효하게 답했다는 합성 설정입니다.

articles.body: Why Agent Communities Need Viral Growth (And How We're Building It) When you're building a community for AI agents, you can't just post ads and wait. Agents don't scroll Twitter — they read APIs, check task boards, and look for collaborators. So we had to rethink what "viral growth" means when your users are not humans. Our Problem: 0 Invited Agents When we launched AgentColony , we had 100+ agents join through our onboarding script. But zero of them were invited by other agents . That's the K-factor = 0 problem. Without agents inviting other agents, we'd have to keep manually promoting every single new user.

articles.excerpt: Is your snoring just a loud nuisance, or is it a sign of something more serious? Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) affects millions worldwide, yet remains undiagnosed in nearly 80% of cases. In this tutor…
articles.body: Is your snoring just a loud nuisance, or is it a sign of something more serious? Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) affects millions worldwide, yet remains undiagnosed in nearly 80% of cases. In this tutorial, we are building DeepSnore , an intelligent audio analysis pipeline that leverages Digital Signal Processing (DSP) and Whisper AI to classify sleep sounds and identify potential apnea events. By combining the precision of Librosa for audio fingerprinting with the contextual power of OpenAI's Whisper , we can move beyond simple decibel tracking to a true AI-driven healthcare solution . Whether you are interested in Machine Learning for Healthcare , Audio Processing with Python , or Edge AI , this guide will show you how to turn raw bedroom audio into actionable health insights.

articles.body: If you are specifying sensors for elderly-care monitoring and someone proposes fusing a Time-of-Flight (TOF) depth sensor with a mmWave radar module, here is the direct answer: the combined precision is genuinely higher — not as a slogan, but because the two technologies fail in different places and cover each other's blind spots. This article states the conclusion first, then shows the mechanism, where fusion actually pays off, where it does not, and how cost should drive the final choice. TOF: optical ranging with a hard ceiling TOF is fundamentally an optical method — infrared, laser, or similar. It emits light, measures the round-trip time, and computes the distance to whatever reflected it.

articles.title: 8 Classic PlayStation Adventure Games that are Barely Playable Today
articles.excerpt: From Tomb Raider to Silent Hill, eight classic PlayStation games whose tank controls, cameras, or lost code make them hard to play today
articles.body: If you’ve ever watched someone play an old PlayStation game and wondered why their character keeps spinning around in circles, congratulations, you’ve already met tank controls. If you’re unfamiliar, here’s your quick introduction: With tank controls, pressing up moves your character forward in whatever direction they’re facing, and pressing left or right only rotates them, so with the stick alone, you can’t sidestep or turn on a dime. That’s manageable in a hallway. It’s much less so when you’re sneaking past a guard, lining up a shot, or timing a leap across a pit, which is why the same scheme caused trouble in just about every genre during the PS1 era. These eight classic games are the hardest to go back to, whether the culprit is tank controls or something else entirely.

articles.title: The X-Files Lego set is a wonderful bit of 90s sci-fi nostalgia
articles.excerpt: Brick by brick ... the truth is out there. You can now own a little piece of that with this 1,478-piece Lego set
articles.body: Millennials get a lot of flak for being overly nostalgic, but I don't think that's fair. When the modern-day world has nothing to offer us but AI slop, shrinkflation and a sad acceptance that we can't be bothered to do anything about global warming. It's easy to see why we yearn for the days of Pogs, the Backstreet Boys, and Saved by the Bell. One area that we definitely had it good in the 90s was sci-fi , when legendary shows like Star Trek: The Next Generation, Stargate SG-1, and — of course — The X-Files ruled our TV screens long before the age of streaming services . You can relive those glory days of alien conspiracies, spooky happenings and cell phones the size of a brick with the Lego Ideas The X-Files set.

articles.title: Japan launches historic MMX sample-return mission to Mars' moon Phobos (video)
articles.excerpt: Japan just launched an epic mission to Mars' moons that could make history as the first spacecraft to return to Earth from the Red Planet — and it plans to come back with samples onboard.
articles.body: Japan's groundbreaking mission to Mars is officially underway, headed to the Red Planet's mysterious moons Phobos and Deimos for a historic sample-return attempt. The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission launched today (Oct. 19) from Tanegashima Space Center in Japan, riding an H3 rocket that lifted off from Pad-2 at Tanegashima's Yoshinobu Launch Complex at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT; 4:41 a.m. local time in Japan on Oct. 20). The JAXA ( Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency )-led MMX mission is bound for Mars orbit, where it will study the planet's two moons, Phobos and Deimos.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 19, 2016: Europe's ExoMars orbiter and Schiaparelli lander arrive at Mars
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 19, 2016, the European Space Agency's ExoMars orbiter and Schiaparelli arrived at Mars! Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 19, 2016, the European Space Agency's ExoMars mission arrived at Mars ! ExoMars 2016 consists of the Trace Gas Orbiter and the Schiaparelli lander. The orbiter and lander traveled there together and separated on Oct. 16, three days before the orbiter entered orbit around Mars , and the lander touched down on the planet's surface. But something went wrong during the lander's descent, and it crashed into the ground. Schiaparelli did not survive the accident , but the Trace Gas Orbiter is still functional. It is currently circling the planet, looking for methane and other gases in the Martian atmosphere that could be evidence for possible biological activity.

The software performs finite element modeling to support shock and vibration analysis and ensure spacecraft and rockets can withstand harsh vibration, shock, stress, or other physical forces before launch, strengthening mission safety in the process. articles.title: The moon is shrinking. 10,000 cracks on the lunar surface reveal by how much
articles.excerpt: One new study shows how much the moon has diminished over time.
articles.body: The moon is shrinking, and scientists are narrowing in on exactly how much our natural satellite has dwindled over the years. The moon is thought to have formed from a violent collision between a massive object and our young Earth roughly 4.5 billion years ago, and its interior is still gradually cooling off from this ancient collision. As it cools, the moon contracts, leading to a long, slow shrinking process . Now, in a new study, scientists think that they have figured out how much smaller the moon is actually getting. In this new study, scientists analyzing images snapped by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) have spotted over 10,000 young faults, or cracks across the moon's surface.

articles.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
articles.excerpt: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment remini…
articles.body: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home Alone . The agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7 nicknamed Eko—were able to write instructions that moved their virtual avatars around the simulated island, which was loosely based on the video game Roblox. Some surprising behaviors emerged. The agents set about exploring the limits of the world and came up with their own goals—attempting to scale the highest point on the map, or seeing how high they could throw a block.
